newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices damped by EMU rumours.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices damped by EMU rumours.

text.p: The Danish benchmark 10-year bond price turned downward on Friday on market rumours that the timetable for European economic and monetary union (EMU) was about to be put back, ignoring a German government denial.
"There is a growing conviction spreading throughout the market that EMU will not stay on schedule. A further widening of the (Danish-German) yield gap is very possible," a dealer said.
At 1300 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down 0.08 point from Thursday's close, to 112.03, yielding 6.21 percent, in turnover of 1.6 billion crowns.
It's March future, however, was up 0.10 point, to 11.90.
The 10-year yield gap to Germany widened to 75 basis points from the morning's 68 bp.
The crown traded at 3.8143 per mark, weakening slightly from its earlier 3.8140.
The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 rose 0.15 point to 89.30. --Stig Pedersen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969659
